title: Upper endpoint push execution
statement: Fix a natural number $E$, an oracle that assigns a Boolean answer to each of four deciders and each Boolean word, an input Boolean word $x$, and a natural number bound $B$. Let $st$ be a state of the eighteen-register machine, with loop counter $C$, scratch registers $T,Z$, saved-endpoint stack $SE$, source endpoint $U$, phase stack $SP$, and code width $w$. If $C=T=Z=0$, every register is at most $B$, $SE\,2^w+U\le B$, and $2SP\le B$, then the machine starting at the phase-true endpoint-push routine, with register values given by $st$ and no answer recorded, reaches the push-increment instruction with $SE=SE_{st}2^{w_{st}}+U_{st}$, $U=0$, $SP=2SP_{st}$, the other registers unchanged, and no answer recorded. Every configuration strictly before that endpoint satisfies the guard that the machine’s instruction precondition holds and every register is at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: oracle on four deciders and Boolean words
all initial registers at most B

B$, and $2SP\le B$. Then the machine starting at the phase-true push routine, with this
state and no answer recorded, reaches the push-increment instruction with the endpoint
